The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 04.12.2022 at about 8.30 p.m. Rajkumar Mariyappan had been proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42X9315 being ridden by its rider by name Ramesh on Yalachipalya Road, near Choukimata Temple,
Yalachipalya, a rider drove the said motor cycle in rash and negligently with high speed, inorder to avoid road pole, applied break suddenly, due SCCH5 to the said impact, both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, Rajkumar Mariyappan was taken to Channapatna Government Hospital, after first aid shifted to NIMHANS Hospital Bengaluru,
thereafter shifted to Basavanagudi Medical Centre Bengaluru, for further management shifted to Victoria Hospital Bengaluru, during the course of treatment he was died on 17.12.2022 and post mortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital Bengaluru.
Mariyappan.K vs Pandu on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72532992/
2 3.
At the time of accident, deceased/Rajkumar Mariyappan was aged about 19 years, hale and healthy, working at Pavithra Praveen Flour Mill, Yalachipalya, Channapatna thereby earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.

petitioner No.1 and 2 are parents of the deceased, SCCH5 petitioner No.3 and 4 are younger brother and sister of the deceased/RajkumarMariyappan, due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners are suffering from mental agony, they have lost moral, social and economical support in a great extent.

Out of this accident crime No.310/2022 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42X9315 before the Channapatna Rural P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338, 304(A) of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is the insurer of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.40,00,000/.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

R2/insurer of motor cycle SCCH5 bearing Reg.No.KA42X9315 has appeared and filed written statement denying the case of the petitioners, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170, 149(2) of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act, further rider of the said motor cycle driven the said motor cycle without having valid and specific endorsement driving license.

Further submitted that, said motor cycle was insured with him vide its policy No.670104312201000012680 valid since 30.10.2022 to 29.10.2023, claim made by the petitioners is higher side, hence their petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
SCCH5 ::ISSUES::
1.Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Rajkumar Mariyappan died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 04.12.2022 at about 8.30 p.m. when deceased was a pillion rider on TVS Jupiter motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42X9315 near Yalachipalya Road, Chowkimata Temple, Channapatna, at that time, the driver of the said TVS Jupiter motor cycle in order to avoid road pole applied break suddenly and deceased succumbed to death and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has deposed his evidence as PW1 and marked SCCH5 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11

On the other hand, there is no evidence of R2.
7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.
Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the Mariyappan.K vs Pandu on 13 February, 2024

3  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 being the father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chiefexamination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of further SCCH5 requisition by police to insert Sec.304(a) of IPC is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
9 . In crossexamination there is no dispute about place, date and time of the accident, further no dispute about negligency of rider of the motor cycle by name Ramesh.
The police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of rider, there is no involvement of any other vehicle.
Under such circumstances, it is clear that, negligency of rider of the motor cycle is proved.
Rider is no party to the petition, owner of the said motor cycle is a party to the petition, but he has not contested the petition inspite of SCCH5 service of notice.
The defence of the R2 is that, rider of the motor cycle by name Ramesh Naik had no driving licence at the time of accident, but copy of driving licence is on record.
It reveals that, since 11.02.2016 Ramesh has driving licence to run the motor cycle.
Under such circumstances, defence taken by the R2 with regard to driving licence is not sustainable.
Considering the same, I have answered the above issue No.1 in the affirmative.
10. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased Rajkumar Mariyappan was aged about 19 years at the time of accident.

In this regard they have produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9 wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 02.05.2004, the alleged accident is occurred on 04.12.2022, hence relying SCCH5 on Ex.P.9

age of the deceased is considered as 19 years at the time of his death and multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working at Pavithra Praveen Flour Mill under one Pandu, thereby earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.
In this regard petitioners have not produced documents with regard to his occupation and income.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202223.
In the case on hand, petitioner is an employee at flour mill, so that, he comes under the unskilled worker category.

Very accident is occurred on 04.12.2022, accordingly as on the date of accident SCCH5 including dearness allowances for unskilled workers minimum wages for a month will come to Rs.13,821/, so that,
said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency 12.

Petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is mother, petitioner No.3 is younger brother,
petitioner No.4 is younger sister of the deceased/Rajkumar Mariyappan.
In order to prove their relationship, they have produced copy of aadhar cards, it reveals that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of Mariyappan.K vs Pandu on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72532992/
4 the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.
SCCH5 13.

In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.13,821/ p.m. hence,
which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 40% with reference to his age.
14. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.13,821/
(ii) 40% of (i) above if Rs.13,821/ (+)
 added to the Rs.5,528/ =
 monthly income as Rs.19,349/
 future prospects

SCCH5 (iii) 1/2 of (ii) of the Rs.19,349/ ()
 same to be deducted Rs.9,675/ =
 towards personal  and living expenses

Monthly income Rs.9,674/ p.m.
(iv) Compensation after Rs.9,674/ x 12 Rs.20,89,584/
 multiplier of 18 is x 18  applied 15.

Hence, petitioner No.1 & 2 being the parents, petitioner No.3 and 4 being brother of the sister of the deceased are entitled for loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/ each, further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/ and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/.
16. Petitioners have produced prescriptions marked as Ex.P.10, medical bills are marked as Ex.P.11 to the tune of Rs.3,40,298/.
There is crossexamination that, bill No.1 of Ex.P.11 for an amount of Rs.1,88,500/ SCCH5 does not bears seal and signature, such question is admitted by PW1.

On perusal of Ex.P.11 it is clear that, said bill does not bears seal and signature, but very bill is supported with the 3 payment receipts for an amount of Rs.30,000/, 1,00,000/ and 58,000/,
which all comes to Rs.1,88,000/.

Under such circumstances, only due to non signing and seal on Mariyappan.K vs Pandu on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72532992/
5 the said document it is not possible to say that, very document is created one.
There are further 23 bills with seal and signature.
Considering the same, objections raised by counsel for R2 during argument with regard to genuineness of the bill is ignored.

In total there is bill of Rs.3,40,298/
with seal and signature.
So that, petitioners are entitled for the said bill.
SCCH5 17.

The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 20,89,58400 2. Loss of filial consortium 1,60,00000 (Rs.40,000/ each to petitioner No.1 to 4)
3 . Loss of Estate 15,00000 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,00000 5.
Medical Expenses 3,40,29800 Total 26,19,88200 18.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.26,19,882/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount,
19.

In the case on hand, R2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing SCCH5 No.67010431220100012680 in respect of of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA42X9315 in favour of R1 which is valid since 30.10.2022 to 29.10.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 04.12.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further rider of the said motor cycle by name Ramesh Naik had valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3
: Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,19,882/ (Rupees Twenty Six Lakhs Nineteen Thousand Eight Hundred Eighty Two Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Mariyappan.K vs Pandu on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72532992/
6
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 30:50:10:10 in the award amount.

The Petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be SCCH5 kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since Petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till they attain age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioners guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
